grades.quote: Luckily RISC-V provides a helping hand in the form of the sscratch register. The csrw instruction at the start of uservec saves a0 in sscratch. Now uservec has one register (a0) to play with.
grades.reason: Directly explains that at the start of uservec, no general-purpose registers are free, so the csrw instruction saves a0 in sscratch, giving uservec a working register; later a0 is retrieved from sscratch and saved in the trapframe.

grades.quote: At the beginning of a trap handler, software normally uses a CSRRW instruction to swap `sscratch` with an integer register to obtain an initial working register.
grades.reason: RISC-V privileged spec description of sscratch, noting that at the start of a trap handler software swaps sscratch with an integer register to get a working register. It matches the role in xv6 but is generic, not xv6-specific.
